text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

-- Like a headhunter, Greenpeace is calling for the resignation of the official who lead the Swiss delegation at the international conference on protection of species. In advertisements and posters, Peter Dollinger, chief of the federal veterinary office, is shown in the crosshair in front of an elephant.
-- Swissair wants to create about 135 to 160 jobs for flight attendants and pilots.
-- Genetically engineered alterations have been found in Yasoya-products of the company Baer. All these products have been recalled from the shops.

-- Christoph Blocher, president of the SVP Swiss People's Party in Zurich, uses advertisements, Internet sites and videotape to talk himself or about Eizenstat report on Switzerland's wartime past. Blocher's omnipresence in the media raises the question whether Adolf Ogi, the defense minister, still represents the SVP.
